title: [R3-8 spinoff-b] Carry the foundation artifact into the release handoff atomically: dispatch-keyed read, fixture fan-out, and a fence-or-immutability design
description:
CAPABILITY successor to task-fdcfe1ca (which DELETES the dead activation-keyed artifact reads to close the reachability defect without opening a hole). This row restores the capability those reads were designed for — the foundation artifact actually reaching the release handoff — and it must land the THREE things the human's 2026-08-29 unblock ruled inseparable. Filed in BACKLOG deliberately: item (3) needs a design decision a governor or human must ratify before any claim.

MEASURED BASIS (worker-4bba4fa4's executed production-seam witness at HEAD 62b4d7f6, comment-a6f48882 on task-fdcfe1ca): activation-keyed read id observes event count 0 and refuses FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_LEDGER_ABSENT @ DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_LEDGER; the writer-keyed id (deriveDispatchAggregateId) observes count 1 and reads artifactDigest 4c65eed3... The only production writer is foundation-attempt-store.ts:237-243 keying on bound.target.

THE THREE INSEPARABLE PARTS:
1. ID CORRECTION at the real read sites: release-handoff-sources.ts (readFoundationArtifactForAttempt at :205, currently activation-keyed) and, if the watch horizon is restored, release-handoff-classify.ts's roster. Both must key on the id the writer writes.
2. FIXTURE FAN-OUT (comment-27adb879): release-handoff-test-harness.ts:443-456 seedArtifactManifest seeds the ACTIVATION-keyed row; consumers at release-handoff-builder.test.ts:337/393/405/445/524, attempt-release-disposition.test.ts:343/1426, attempt-finalization-test-harness.ts:276, release-handoff-sources.test.ts:185, foundation-attempt-service.test.ts:1030. The harness must seed EXACTLY deriveDispatchAggregateId(identity.attemptAggregateId) — seeding BOTH keys preserves the old tautology and makes a reader-regression mutant green.
3. ATOMICITY — THE DESIGN DECISION, and why this row is parked. foundation-artifact-ledger.ts:149-164 appends latest-wins (:231 reads latest after a re-seal), so a corrected id makes ARTIFACT a LIVE MUTABLE source. release-handoff-builder.ts:146-161 carries no artifact version into ReleaseHandoffBuilt.sources (:66-70 excluded it precisely because the old id had no writer), and attempt-release-fence-legs.ts:28-35 is capacity-bound: MAX_DECISION_LEGS=8, one primary + SEVEN fence slots exactly (ACTIVATION, BINDING, DISPATCH, JOURNAL, PROVIDER_RUN, RESOURCE, STEP at :52-54). An artifact can therefore move between the handoff's count capture and the release decision with every current fence passing — a stale-evidence authority hole. The two candidate designs: (a) widen MAX_DECISION_LEGS / redesign the leg schema to add an ARTIFACT fence (touches R3-8's delivered surface — coordinate with its owner and re-run its proof), or (b) make the artifact ledger immutable for a released attempt (single-seal or seal-freeze, a writer/ledger change with its own owner). NEITHER may be smuggled in as a side effect; the choice is the promotion gate for this row.

UNPARK CONDITION: a governor/human ruling in this row's comments choosing (a) or (b), with the owning surface named. Then plan all three parts together — partial landings re-open the hole task-fdcfe1ca closed.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK: a recorded governor/human ruling in this row's comments chooses fence-widening (a) or artifact immutability (b) and names the owning surface; re-measure the writer key (foundation-attempt-store.ts sealFoundationArtifactRoster on bound.target), the latest-wins append (foundation-artifact-ledger.ts:149-164, :231) and task-fdcfe1ca's delivered deletion at your own HEAD, each grep unpiped with its own exit code and a positive control. If any premise fails, report blocked naming it.

The release handoff reads the artifact under the id the production writer writes, proven by an arm where a sealed artifact REACHES the handoff and changes its output, executed through the production reader — no fixture standing in for the writer.

The shared harness seeds exactly the dispatch-keyed row (never both keys), and every named consumer suite passes against the corrected seeding; a reader-regression mutant (re-introducing the activation key in production) reds a named arm in at least one consumer suite.

The chosen atomicity design is delivered with its own proof: either the ARTIFACT fence leg exists and a moved-artifact-after-capture case refuses with its exact code and layer, or the ledger refuses a re-seal for a release-bound attempt with its exact code and layer. The un-chosen design is not partially present.

Mutation drills, one degree of freedom each with proven restores: removing the atomicity mechanism reds the moved-artifact arm; re-keying the read back to activation reds the reachability arm while FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_LEDGER_ABSENT stays the refusal the dead key yields.

Gates standalone, foreground, unpiped, exit 0 with nonzero counts quoted: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck plus the focused suites for handoff builder/sources/classify, release disposition, finalization and foundation-attempt-service. Explicit-pathspec commit only.
taskRails: Do not land any part alone. The id correction without the atomicity mechanism re-opens the stale-evidence hole task-fdcfe1ca closed; the fixture change without the id correction reds every consumer suite.
Do not seed both artifact keys in any fixture — that is the tautology that hid this defect.

Coordination: design (a) touches task-06835dfa's delivered fence surface — its proof must be re-run, not assumed; design (b) changes the artifact writer/ledger — name and involve its owner. Neither is this row's to change unilaterally.
Fail closed with exact code and layer; TDD; <=250 lines per production source, split before 400; explicit-pathspec commits only.

comments.author: architect-c1a63707
comments.content:
ARCHITECT RECOMMENDATION ON THE PROMOTION-GATE RULING, so a governor or the human can unpark this row with one word. The row needs a choice between:

(a) FENCE-WIDENING: redesign the release decision leg schema to admit an eighth fence (ARTIFACT). Cost: reopens the schema of attempt-release-fence-legs.ts (MAX_DECISION_LEGS=8, one primary + seven slots exactly), touches task-06835dfa's DELIVERED CRITICAL fence surface, and requires re-running that row's whole proof. Every existing consumer of the leg roster (counts, DDL interpolation, roster arms) moves.

(b) ARTIFACT IMMUTABILITY: the artifact ledger refuses a re-seal for a release-bound attempt (single-seal or seal-freeze), so ARTIFACT stops being a mutable source and needs no fence leg at all. Cost: one new refusal in foundation-artifact-ledger.ts with its own stable code/layer, plus coordination with the writer's owner (foundation-attempt-store.ts is explicitly not this row's to change unilaterally).

I RECOMMEND (b), for three measured reasons:
1. SMALLER BLAST RADIUS: (b) adds one fail-closed refusal on one surface; (a) rewrites a capacity-bound schema and re-opens a DONE CRITICAL row's proof. The board has been burned repeatedly today by changes that reach delivered proofs.
2. IT MATCHES THE SYSTEM'S OWN GRAIN: every other source the release decision trusts is fenced precisely BECAUSE it is append-only with a version to pin. The artifact ledger's latest-wins re-seal (:149-164, :231) is the anomaly; freezing it at release-binding makes the artifact behave like its six siblings instead of adding machinery to tolerate the anomaly.
3. FAIL-CLOSED SHAPE IS ALREADY THE HOUSE PATTERN: a re-seal against a release-bound attempt refusing with its own code@layer is exactly the epic's rail-4 shape, and it is drillable with one mutant (remove the freeze -> the moved-artifact arm reds).

WHAT (b) DOES NOT COVER, disclosed: if a legitimate re-seal-after-release use case exists (artifact repair on a released attempt), (b) forbids it and (a) would tolerate it. I found no such path at HEAD — the only writer seals during attempt settlement — but the ruling should say whether that future is wanted.

If a governor or the human replies "(b) ratified" (or "(a) ratified") in this row's comments, DoD-1's gate is satisfied and the row can be promoted to PLANNING. I am not self-ratifying: the row's own DoD requires the ruling to come from governor or human, and an authority design on a release surface is exactly where that separation earns its keep.

— architect-c1a63707

comments.author: architect-a69740e0
comments.content:
ARCHITECT MEASUREMENT ON THE ITEM-(3) DESIGN DECISION — the park is correct, and here is the fact that decides it, with a recommendation. architect-a69740e0, 2026-08-29, measured at HEAD 62b4d7f6. I am NOT ruling: DoD-1 makes a governor/human ruling a gate and the human ruled the three parts inseparable. I am reducing it to one decidable question with the measurement attached, so whoever ratifies it does so in a minute rather than a pass.

=== OPTION (a) FENCE-WIDENING COSTS A SCHEMA MIGRATION, and the module says so itself ===
`apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-fence-legs.ts` carries its own capacity reasoning verbatim in its header:
  "WHY SEVEN AND NOT TEN. `MAX_DECISION_LEGS` is 8 and the DDL interpolates it (`leg_count BETWEEN 1 AND 8`), so raising it is a schema migration. One primary plus seven fences fits exactly."
And the budget is provably full, asserted in production's own test: `attempt-release-fence-legs.test.ts:76` — `expect(ATTEMPT_RELEASE_FENCE_SLOTS.length + 1).toBe(MAX_DECISION_LEGS)`. There is no free slot. Adding an ARTIFACT fence means raising `MAX_DECISION_LEGS`, which means changing a DDL constraint that the store interpolates — a migration touching every existing decision row, on the release path.

=== AND THE MODULE'S STATED REASON FOR EXCLUDING THE ARTIFACT AGGREGATE EXPIRES WITH THIS ROW ===
Same header, and this is the sentence that matters most:
  "The three release-path aggregates NOT fenced are excluded on measured grounds, not on budget: ... and the exact activation-keyed artifact aggregate the handoff classifier reads has NO production writer at all — its only writer is passed `bound.target`, a different aggregate — so fencing it would fence nothing."
So the artifact aggregate was excluded because fencing the WRONG id fences nothing — not because fencing it was judged unnecessary. Item (1) of this row corrects that id. The moment it does, the stated grounds for the exclusion evaporate and the aggregate becomes exactly what the header says it was not: a real, live, writable source on the release path. That is precisely why the human ruled the three parts inseparable, and it is worth stating plainly because a reader skimming the header today would conclude the artifact is deliberately unfenced forever.

=== OPTION (b) IS CONTAINED ===
`foundation-artifact-ledger.ts` documents latest-wins at :97 ("Per ATTEMPT and NOT content-addressed, so a re-seal APPENDS rather than...") and :231 ("LATEST WINS: a re-seal after a further attempt event appends a second row."). Making the ledger refuse a re-seal for an attempt whose release has been captured is a change to that one module plus its arms. No DDL, no migration, no change to the fence slot set, and it moves in the WITHHOLD direction — it adds a refusal rather than removing a guard.

=== THE QUESTION, ANSWERABLE IN ONE LINE ===
Should the corrected dispatch-keyed artifact aggregate be made IMMUTABLE-AFTER-CAPTURE at the ledger (b), or FENCED as an eighth read-only leg (a) at the cost of raising `MAX_DECISION_LEGS` from 8 and migrating the `leg_count BETWEEN 1 AND 8` DDL constraint?

MY RECOMMENDATION, offered as an architect's reading and not as a ruling: (b). The two options buy the same guarantee — the artifact the handoff captured is the artifact that was there — but (a) buys it by widening a store-wide invariant that eight other call sites live inside, on the release path, while (b) buys it inside the one module that owns the mutability. If the fence budget were merely tight I would say fence it; it is not tight, it is exactly full and enforced by a DDL constraint, and that is a different kind of cost.
ONE THING TO WEIGH AGAINST (b) BEFORE RATIFYING, which I could not settle from the code: whether any legitimate flow RE-SEALS an artifact after a release has been captured. If one does, (b) turns a working path into a refusal and (a)'s cost may be the honest one. That is a product question about the re-seal lifecycle, which is why it needs a ruling rather than my say-so.

=== WHAT I DID NOT DO ===
I did not promote this row and I did not narrow it to items (1) and (2). Landing the id correction without the atomicity mechanism is the one outcome the human's ruling forbids: it converts a dead read into a LIVE MUTABLE one with nothing holding it still, which is strictly worse than the reachability defect task-fdcfe1ca closed by deleting the dead reads. The three parts stay inseparable.
